title: Hosted inference surface: Slimline PRD + acceptance bundle and launch checklist
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Slimline PRD that defines a minimal behavioral contract and acceptance bundle for the hosted inference surface (chat/completions/embeddings/rerank). Consolidates acceptance tests, rollout schedule, and operational runbooks to accelerate a low-friction launch for PLG customers while preserving compatibility guarantees for enterprise customers.
problem_statement: Product teams require a succinct, testable contract for our hosted endpoints that balances minimal surface area with predictable semantics across generation, streaming, embeddings, and reranking. Current PRDs are large and fragmented, blocking QA and delaying go-live windows. We need a focused PRD and checklist to enable a reliable, auditable launch with clear rollback criteria.
goals: Define a minimal, deterministic behavioral contract for chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank endpoints
Provide a reproducible acceptance test bundle that QA and SRE can run pre-launch
Specify canary rollout and automated rollback triggers tied to SLOs and quality metrics
Ensure billing and telemetry (token-level latency/cost) are instrumented prior to GA
Ship a launch checklist that reduces cross-team handoffs and explicitly lists sign-offs
non_goals: Extensive API surface expansion (no new endpoint types beyond the four named)
Major model architecture changes or new model onboarding during this launch
Full enterprise feature parity (RBAC, advanced KMS bindings) which will be delivered in follow-ups
scope: Behavioral contracts and example payloads for chat, completions, embeddings, rerank
Acceptance test harness (synthetic prompt sets + golden outputs) and CI gates
Launch checklist including security, observability, docs, and SDK compatibility tests
Canary rollout plan with explicit thresholds and escalation path
Telemetry dashboards for per-route latency, error rate, and token cost
api_surface: POST /v1/completions - minimal required fields: model, prompt; optional: max_tokens, temperature, top_p, stream boolean
POST /v1/chat - messages array, model; support for streaming and function-calling disabled for this minimal launch
POST /v1/embeddings - input (string | list<string>), model; batching supported
POST /v1/rerank - candidate list, query, model; response: scores array and optional metadata
technical_requirements: Stable backward-compatible payload format for all four endpoints
Streaming responses must emit final EOF event and proper delta sections per current SDK conventions
Per-route token accounting available via event traces and ingested into cost dashboard
Synthetic golden-set runner in CI that can be executed against staging and a small canary cluster
Graceful fallback: if primary model returns error 5xx or exceeds latency threshold, route to compatible lighter-weight variant
Rate limiting and quota behavior must be documented and simulated in QA
acceptance_criteria: Functional: All endpoints accept and validate the minimal payloads; invalid payloads return 4xx with consistent error schema
Behavioral: For the provided golden prompt set, streaming and non-streaming paths produce semantically equivalent final outputs within defined similarity thresholds
Performance: 95th percentile end-to-end latency for completions <= 400ms on canary traffic profile; chat 95p <= 550ms
Scalability: Embeddings batch path can process 64 inputs concurrently with no more than 10% tail latency regression vs baseline
Reliability: Error budget consumption during canary (72h window) must be below 1% for all routes
Fallback: Canary test where primary model is disabled must succeed by routing to fallback with documented quality delta
Billing: Token-level costs show up in the cost dashboard for canary traffic and match expected billing model
Telemetry: Per-request trace and token breakdown emitted and searchable within observability UI for 7-day retention
Security: Penetration sanity checks and SSO gating complete; secrets and keys validated against KMS policy
Docs: OpenAPI snippets and SDK examples for each endpoint exist in docs repo and render correctly
launch_checklist: Engineering sign-off: all acceptance criteria green in staging and canary
QA sign-off: golden-set pass and fuzz testing completed
SRE sign-off: alerts, runbooks, and escalation paths reviewed; smoke test automation enabled
Security sign-off: security checklist and SSO/KMS review complete
Billing & Usage: token accounting validated; quota controls tested
Docs: API reference, quickstarts, and changelog published
SDKs: minimal SDK examples validated for Python and Node
Partner comms: customer-facing release notes prepared and channel comms scheduled
Rollout plan scheduled in calendar with stakeholders and on-call rotations assigned
Canary config deployed to 5% of traffic for first 24h, subject to automated checks
rollout_plan: Day 0: deploy to staging; smoke tests run automatically; manual sign-off by PM and ENG leads
Day 1-3: canary 5% traffic; automated golden-set checks run hourly; monitor SLOs and quality metrics
Day 4: increase canary to 25% if canary window shows no regression and error budget intact
Day 5-7: 50% progressive ramp with nightly automated regression suites
Day 8: if stable, full ramp to 100% with monitoring hold and post-launch retrospective scheduled
metrics_and_alerts: Token throughput and per-token cost estimates
Similarity score distribution for golden-set outputs (embedding cosine and generation n-gram overlap)
Canary deviation alert: any metric > 2x baseline alerting immediately to on-call
Data quality alert: sudden drop in embedding vector norms or high rerank score dispersion
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Golden-set overfitting causing false pass. Mitigation: include synthetic adversarial prompts and customer-sourced examples
Risk: Fallback model has unacceptable quality delta. Mitigation: explicit fallback quality gate and opt-out toggle per-customer
Risk: Unexpected billing discrepancies. Mitigation: run parallel billing simulation and reconcile before GA
Risk: Streaming SDK mismatch. Mitigation: lock streaming contract and add backward-compat test in CI
open_questions: Should function-calling remain off by default for chat in the minimal surface?
What is the canonical similarity threshold for considering embeddings 'equivalent' in acceptance tests?
Do we enable per-tenant fallback controls at launch or delay to dedicated capacity roadmap?
What guardrails do we expose in the console for canary ramp adjustments?
